To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PCNA and Ki-67 are both independent prognostic markers for progression of prostate cancer.
PCNA and Ki-67 are not independent prognostic markers for prostate cancer progression, and that PCNA is not a better prognostic marker than Ki-67.
PCNA is a useful marker of cell proliferation and that the expression of PCNA in prostate cancer is a prognostic marker for progression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the determination of the proliferation rate in prostatic cancer using the monoclonal antibody Ki‐67.
the study of the role of PCNA in the regulation of cell proliferation.
the development of new methods for the detection and quantitation of DNA and RNA in the cells of the prostate and their application to the diagnosis of prostate disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PCNA is a reliable prognostic marker for prostate cancer and that it is a good predictor for the prognosis of prostate cancer patients.
the use of PCNA as a prognostic marker should be discouraged.
PCNA is an independent prognosticator in men with localized prostate cancer and that it is superior to Ki-67.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PCNA assay has been used as a surrogate marker for the proliferative activity of a cell and has been shown to have prognostic significance in many cancers.
we have identified a new class of small molecules that can modulate the expression of a number of genes involved in the regulation of cell growth and proliferation.
we have shown that Ki‐67 and PCNA are both useful markers of tumour cell proliferation and that they are both independent predictors of tumour recurrence after radical prostatectomy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proliferation rate of the tumor, measured by PCNA, is an independent predictor of prostate cancer recurrence and survival, even after adjusting for other known prognostic factors such as Gleason score, PSA, and margin status.
PCNA can be used as an independent prognos- tic factor in prostate cancer.
Ki‐67 is a good predictor of prostate cancer aggressiveness.
